drive.io-local.lock-per-home.why: A second project's home saw another home's runner as live, started nothing, and its board sat in the gate with no runner.

proves.claim: serveLocalRunner returns served false with a refusal code and a next line when the same home already holds the lock.

drive.io-local.same-home-refusal-typed.why: A bare pid left the command layer nothing typed to print when the same home already runs a local runner.

proves.claim: serveRunner posts place { host, root } with each claim action, root being its cache folder.

drive.claim-place.claim-sends-place.why: Without the place the board cannot tell two runner ids on one machine and folder apart from two machines.

proves.claim: A claim answered with RUNNER_DUPLICATE ends serveRunner with that error and runs no job.

drive.claim-place.duplicate-ends-serve.why: Without it a duplicate runner would retry forever and each id would still take slots on the machine.

proves.claim: With serve.restartTrial on, a new process whose trial p95 is over 1 s or over twice the old p95, or whose CPU is over twice the old, leaves the old process listening with no handoff and one log line naming both p95s and the commit.

drive.io-fresh.trial-keeps-old.why: A slow new commit would otherwise take the serve's socket and make every runner claim slow.

proves.claim: A trial within its thresholds hands the socket over as before, and with the setting off no trial runs and nothing changes.

drive.io-fresh.trial-passes-hands-over.why: The guard must not delay or block restarts that are fine, and must be inert when off.

proves.claim: restartOnCodeMove runs trialClaims over a scratch board of the live shape before the handoff: claims delayed 2 s each are refused and undelayed claims hand over.

drive.io-fresh.trial-real-claims.why: The thresholds are judged on real rolled-back claims over a board with tens of thousands of gate shard rows, not on stubbed figures alone.
